title: U.S. House · Maine's 2nd District
area: Northern, western, and central Maine, including Lewiston, Bangor, and Aroostook County — geographically most of the state outside greater Portland.

context.text: Incumbent Jared Golden (D), first elected in 2018, did not seek re-election, leaving the seat open for the first time since 2014.

Donald Trump carried the 2nd District 53.5%-44.5% over Kamala Harris in 2024, while Golden won re-election in the district 50.3%-49.7% the same year; Republicans consider the open seat a pickup opportunity in 2026.

Matthew Dunlap defeated Joe Baldacci, Paige Loud, and Jordan Wood in the Democratic primary. Paul LePage, Maine's former governor, won the Republican primary unopposed after James Clark did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Matthew Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District and the sitting Maine State Auditor. A former journalist and columnist, he served in the Maine House, as Secretary of State in two separate stretches, and ran for U.S. Senate in 2012; he won the 2026 Democratic primary after a ranked-choice runoff.

background.text: Born and raised in Bar Harbor, Maine, and graduated from Mount Desert Island High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history (1987) and a master's degree in English literature (1994) from the University of Maine; also completed Harvard University's Senior Executives in State and Local Government program.

Worked for 25 years as a journalist and columnist for The Northwoods Sporting Journal and other publications, and for nearly a year as executive director of the Sportsman's Alliance of Maine; also worked in commercial food service, nonprofit administration, textiles, and farming.
Served in the Maine House of Representatives from 1996 to 2004, representing Old Town (District 121), and chaired the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife.

Elected Maine Secretary of State by the Legislature in 2004 and served 2005-2011; selected again in 2012 and served 2013-2021. Served as president of the National Association of Secretaries of State from 2010 to 2011.
Finished second in the 2012 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, behind Cynthia Dill.
Elected State Auditor by the Legislature in December 2020, served briefly in 2021, and was selected again on November 14, 2022.

Announced a Democratic primary challenge to Rep. Jared Golden in October 2025; Golden announced in November 2025 he would not seek re-election. Dunlap won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary in a ranked-choice runoff.
Founding board member of the Maine Youth Fish and Game Association and a past member of the University of Maine Board of Visitors and the Bangor Symphony Orchestra board; lives in Old Town, Maine.

priorities.text: Says he is running to stand up to the Trump administration and to fight for affordable healthcare, a lower cost of living, and higher wages.
priorities.quote: Mainers deserve a fighter who won't cave to Donald Trump. ... When I'm in Congress, I'll stand up for Maine, and I'll fight for affordable healthcare, a lower cost of living, and higher wages for hardworking people.

priorities.text: On healthcare, says he wants to re-establish ACA tax credits but sees Medicare for All as the broader goal.
priorities.quote: re-establish [ACA] tax credits, but overall, I think the real answer is Medicare-for-All and just cut to the chase.

positions.summary: Supports restoring ACA tax credits in the near term and says Medicare for All is the longer-term goal.
positions.quote: re-establish [ACA] tax credits, but overall, I think the real answer is Medicare-for-All and just cut to the chase.

record.text: Elected Maine State Auditor in 2022 (with a brief earlier appointment in 2021); the position audits state government finances.
Served as Maine Secretary of State from 2005-2011 and 2013-2021.

summary.text: Paul LePage is the Republican nominee for Maine's 2nd Congressional District. A business executive and turnaround consultant, he served on the Waterville City Council, as mayor of Waterville, and as Governor of Maine for two terms (2011-2019). He lost a 2022 comeback bid for governor and was unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born October 9, 1948, in Lewiston, Maine, the eldest of 18 children; according to his campaign website, he left home at age 11 and was homeless before two families took him in.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Husson College (1971) and an M.B.A. from the University of Maine (1975).
Worked in business for a lumber company in New Brunswick, Canada, and Scott Paper Company, and founded the management consulting firm LePage & Kasevich Inc. in the 1980s.
Hired in 1996 as general manager of Marden's, a Maine discount retail chain.
Elected to the Waterville City Council in 1997 and re-elected in 1999; served until 2002.
Elected mayor of Waterville in 2003, re-elected in 2008, and served from 2004 until January 2011.
Elected Governor of Maine in 2010 and re-elected in 2014 with 48.2% of the vote; served from 2011 to 2019. According to his campaign website, he was Maine's first Franco-American governor.
Ran for a third non-consecutive term as governor in 2022, losing to Democrat Janet Mills, 56% to 42%.
Was unopposed in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary for the open 2nd District seat.

priorities.text: Campaigns on his record as governor, citing a lower unemployment rate, reduced state spending, addressing hospital debt, the state's largest tax cut, welfare reform, and increased K-12 spending.
Says he would help end wasteful federal spending and secure the border, while protecting Social Security and Medicare.
priorities.quote: I'll help President Trump end waste and fraud and secure our borders. Let's lower the cost of electricity and everyday items by ending Biden's inflation policies, bring our northern Maine economy back, help end the woke extremism — putting boys in girls sports, protect our freedoms like the Second Amendment, secure our hospitals ... [and] always protect social security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says he would protect Second Amendment freedoms.
positions.quote: protect our freedoms like the Second Amendment

record.text: As Governor of Maine (2011-2019), his campaign says he lowered the state's unemployment rate, reduced state spending, addressed hospital debt, implemented what he describes as the state's largest tax cut, and reformed welfare.

summary.text: Gregory Ward is a certified write-in Independent candidate for Maine's 2nd Congressional District. Public records show little about his background beyond an earlier run for the Maine House.

background.text: Ran as an Independent for Maine House of Representatives District 148 in 2014, receiving 14.6% (506 votes) in the general election.
Is running in 2026 as an Independent write-in candidate for U.S. House in Maine's 2nd District.

researchNotes: Open seat: incumbent Jared Golden did not seek re-election. This is one of 23 U.S. House districts nationwide that Democrats are defending that Trump carried in 2024, per Ballotpedia's analysis. No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey, or news profile was found for Gregory Ward, so his birthplace, education, and career are not known. Matthew Dunlap's campaign site could not be loaded; his biography relies on Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, and AP.
